AUTHOR: Wang, GA; Hwang, JN; Williams, K; Wallace, F; Rose, CS
TITLE: Shrinking Encoding with Two-Level Codebook Learning for Fine-Grained Fish Recognition
VENUE: 2016 ICPR 2ND WORKSHOP ON COMPUTER VISION FOR ANALYSIS OF UNDERWATER IMAGERY (CVAUI 2016)
REGION: NR (NOAA Alaska Fisheries Science Center Cam-trawl data)
SPECIES: eulachon, walleye pollock, rockfish, salmon, squid
DATA: Cam-trawl dataset (mid-water trawl stereo camera); also Chute multi-spectral dataset (43 classes)
V_EV: no statement found (only generic Introduction remark on light attenuation)
D_EV: Sec. III.A: 'In our evaluation, the standard 10-folds cross-validation is adopted.'
R_EV: Sec. III: each dataset evaluated separately by 10-fold CV; 'We also test the proposed method by using 10-folds cross-validation.'
C_EV: Sec. II: 'a linear SVM classifier is trained and used for fish recognition' — no per-instance score threshold or reject option
E_EV: Table II: only 'Accuracy Compared with Different Methods' (Acc %, mAP %) reported
ARCH: Dense SIFT + bag-of-features with two-level codebook shrinking encoding (ScSPM/LLC) + linear SVM
NOTE: Cam-trawl (in-trawl camera) qualifies as field imagery; Chute multi-spectral dataset is an on-deck chute (not underwater) and was not used for coding. Fish crops detected by GMM, classes include squid (non-fish). Region not stated explicitly; ENV not stated (mid-water trawl).
